newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY OFFERS DEDASZ ELECTRICITY STAKE FOR COUPONS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY OFFERS DEDASZ ELECTRICITY STAKE FOR COUPONS.

text.p: Hungary will offer an eight percent stake in DEDASZ, the regional electricity supplier for South-West Hungary, for compensation coupons in October, the state privatisation agency APV said on Monday.

In allocating shares in Titasz, APV will give preference to domestic and non-resident coupon holders, local municipalities, agricultural producers and companies set up to utilise coupons, APV deputy CEO Miklos Kamaras told a news conference.
The subscriptions will begin on October 7 and APV will close them on October 24, or when the package, which has a face value of 2.38 billion forints, is oversubscribed.
Compensation coupons were awarded to victims of expropriations and persecution under Hungary's former communist and fascist regimes.

A 47.25 percent stake in DEDASZ is held by Germany's Bayernwerk AG, which has the right to acquire a majority in DEDASZ. A 14.58 percent stake is owned by local municipalities, with the rest of the shares held by APV.
Hungary has already sold stakes in four regional electricity suppliers for compensation coupons earlier this year.
APV plans to offer shares in the Budapest electricity supplier Elmu Rt later this year, Kamaras said.
